topic.title: Explicit and Implicit Regularization in Neural Learning
topic.overview: Regularization influences which solution a learning algorithm selects among models that fit the data. This topic examines explicit penalties, data transformations, stochastic depth, gradient geometry, reparameterization, and optimizer-induced biases. It asks how these mechanisms shape generalization rather than assuming that optimization alone reliably prefers useful solutions.
topic.whyItMatters: Training accuracy cannot distinguish a robust pattern from a complicated fit that happens to match the sample. Understanding regularization helps explain dependence on initialization and training history, while clarifying that a useful bias in one setting may suppress necessary structure in another.
topic.evolution: A 1994 analysis relates invariant data augmentation to regularized objectives. In 2020, experiments show that unregularized SGD can reach poorly generalizing solutions after random-label pretraining, challenging a simple implicit-bias explanation. Later representatives study sharpness and gradient penalties; 2026 work connects reparameterization, weight decay, and adaptive learning rates to stable sparse optimization.
openQuestions: Which regularization effects survive changes in training history and architecture?
How can sparsity and invariance be encouraged without removing task-relevant information?
